verdict.line: You lose if you stand and trade autos at range while Jayce freely swaps into Cannon stance; you win by poking with Q's longer reach, shielding with E, and collapsing once his Hammer-stance E (Thundering Blow) is down.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench's Q (Tongue Lash) has 900 range, outreaching Jayce's Cannon-stance Shock Blast at 600 — Tahm can chip, slow, heal off, and stack Acquired Taste from a distance Jayce physically cannot answer with his own poke. Jayce's only tool to stop a close-range engage is Hammer-stance E (Thundering Blow), a single-target knockback on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown; once that's on cooldown he has no way to create space from a melee bruiser with sustain, which is exactly why this sits at 55.3% over 208 games with both lane and solo-kill advantage favoring Tahm.

theirWindow.when: Jayce in Cannon stance, E (Acceleration Gate) up
theirWindow.what: He'll poke from 600 range with Shock Blast and can run an Acceleration Gate to boost its range/speed/damage further — don't walk up for a trade here, just absorb it with Thick Skin's passive stored damage.

yourWindow.when: His Hammer-stance E (Thundering Blow) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Dive with W (Abyssal Dive) to knock him up, then Q repeatedly — each hit stacks Acquired Taste and the 3rd stuns and consumes them, letting you Devour (R) him with nothing left to push you off.

start.why: Run with Health Potion (52.9% over 210 games, 81.7% pick) — the passive block and regen directly answer Jayce's auto-reliant poke pattern while you farm up to level 3.

boots.why: 56.4% win rate over 179 games and the clear majority pick (71.9%) — Jayce's damage is almost entirely physical (autos, Q leap/blast), so flat reduction on every hit matters more than the raw move speed from Swiftness.

core.why: Stacks max health off champion autos — directly scales your passive's bonus damage and your Thick Skin shield pool while you're already poking with Q.
Paired with Heartsteel in the single most-played line into this matchup (56.3% across the recorded builds); keeps your resistances up through the stance-dance poke phase.
Best-performing third item in the sample (66.7% over 15 games) — boosts the healing from Q, Thick Skin, and Devour against a lane with no hard CC to punish the sustain.

runes.keystoneWhy: Most-picked page into this matchup (47% pick, 58.9% win rate) — the bonus health from every proc stacks directly into your passive's max-health scaling and heals through Jayce's chip damage every 4 seconds of contact.

summoners.why: Highest win rate and most-picked combo into Jayce (62% over 49.2% pick) — Ignite punishes his lack of sustain once you land a stacked all-in, converting your solo-kill advantage into an actual kill instead of a reset.

playing.title: Track his stance before engaging
playing.detail: Hammer stance means his E (Thundering Blow) can knock you back on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown; Cannon stance means he's poking from 600 range with Shock Blast and has no knockback available. Only commit to a dive when he's in Cannon stance or his E is visibly down.

playing.title: Poke first with 900-range Q
playing.detail: Your Q (Tongue Lash) outreaches his Cannon-stance Q by 300 units. Throw it from max range to build Acquired Taste stacks and heal off the hit before he's close enough to answer.

playing.title: Hold E for the shield, not the heal
playing.detail: Thick Skin passively stores damage you take and heals you out of combat, but pop the active shield right before he unloads Lightning Field or an Acceleration Gate-boosted Shock Blast so the stored damage doesn't go to waste.

playing.title: All-in only at 3 stacks with his E down
playing.detail: W (Abyssal Dive) to knock him up, Q to land the stun once stacks hit 3, then R (Devour) to lock him down and finish — this sequence is unanswerable if Thundering Blow is on cooldown.

playing.title: Don't facecheck his Cannon poke
playing.detail: Per the matchup read, he'll out-damage you at range and push you off with E when you close distance carelessly — farm safely with Q and wait for your jungler rather than forcing extended trades without minion cover.

playing.title: Build health, not just armor
playing.detail: Heartsteel's stacking directly increases your passive's bonus damage, so every champion auto you land in lane is compounding value beyond the trade itself.

playing.title: Respect his R transform at level 6
playing.detail: Mercury Cannon's first attack strips armor/MR and Mercury Hammer's first attack adds bonus magic damage — expect a harder single trade right after he hits 6, then your own R comes online to answer it.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, item paths, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the ability breakdowns, timings, and tactical reasoning are my own read of the matchup.
